---
title: "Installation"
subtitle: "spp ships as a Claude Code plugin."
---

## Requirements

- **[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)** — spp is a plugin that runs inside it.
- **Python 3.11+** — for the runner scripts spp generates and executes (scoring, splitting).
- A **task model** reachable from your environment — the model the produced prompt will run
  against (any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or a local server).

## Install from the marketplace

From inside Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add JayLBean/supervised-prompt-producer
/plugin install spp@supervised-prompt-producer
```

That registers the `spp` plugin and its `/spp:run` entrypoint.

## Local development

To run against an unreleased or locally-modified version:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/JayLBean/supervised-prompt-producer.git
cd supervised-prompt-producer
claude --plugin-dir ./
```

`--plugin-dir ./` loads the plugin from the working tree, so any local edits take effect on the
next Claude Code session.

## Verify

In a Claude Code session, confirm the entrypoint is available:

```
/spp:run
```

With no task name, the designer agent begins the consultation and asks for one. (See
[Usage](usage.qmd) for the full walkthrough.) If the command is not found, re-check the
`/plugin install` step above, or that `--plugin-dir` points at the cloned repository root.

## What spp writes to your project

spp operates on a `spp/<task-name>/` directory inside your project — the plan, baseline, splits,
per-iteration artifacts, the frozen prompt, and the report all live there. Nothing is written
outside that directory without your approval, and the sacred test set is never read until you
approve gate **G5**.
